# Native versus integrate: what ADX builds, connects to, and leaves alone

Written for B6.2 on 2026-10-17, after the PRD and phases 0–5, against the scope the build actually needed. Each row says who the capability serves, what it costs to keep, and what was decided. "Native" means ADX owns the record and the behaviour. "Integrate" means ADX reads or writes it through a connector and the other system stays the owner. "Not built" means ADX will not have it, with the reason.

| Capability | Decision | User value | Maintenance | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enquiries, people, opportunities, stages | Native (B5.1) | The sales team's record of a buyer is one place, with ADX's score, brief and history beside it. | Our schema, our migrations; the import from GoHighLevel keeps running and reports conflicts. | GoHighLevel stages were being hand-moved and the funnel definition drifted (reference.md). Owning the record is the only way the score and the history agree. |
| Follow-up tasks | Native (B5.1) | A task is created once per occurrence from the brief's recommended step and shows on the opportunity. | One table, one state machine, no sync. | A task tied to ADX's own recommendation has nowhere else to live; a board in GoHighLevel would need a two-way sync for little gain. |
| Pipeline board | Native, minimal (B5.1 `/pipeline`) | Owner and stage per opportunity, versioned edits. | A list view; no drag-and-drop, no custom columns. | The team needs to see and change stage and owner. A full board clone of GoHighLevel is a product of its own; the value stops at stage and owner. |
| Review and approval | Native (B2/B3 proposals, B5.4 supervisor inbox) | Every outside write and every send passes a person, with the evidence and the policy decision beside it. | The proposal and recommendation tables already carry it. | Approval is the safety boundary of the whole system; it cannot be delegated to another tool's UI. |
| Schedules | Native, as jobs (River periodic jobs, research schedules) | Reports, refreshes, scoring and arbitration run on time without an operator. | Cron-style entries in `cmd/adx`; one table for research schedules. | A scheduling product would add an integration for what a periodic job already does. No user-facing scheduler UI is built; the schedules are configuration. |
| Lead ingestion and custom fields | Integrate (GoHighLevel read; field outbox write under policy) | Leads keep arriving where the team works; ADX's score reaches the field they read. | Provider client, webhook, outbox with echo and conflict detection. | GoHighLevel stays the inbox of record for forms and WhatsApp-origin leads; rebuilding capture would re-create a product the team already pays for. |
| Ad delivery and bidding | Integrate (Google Ads, Meta reads; budget, status and paused-campaign writes under policy) | Figures and controlled changes with caps and approval. | Two provider clients, versioned APIs, token rotation. | ADX will never deliver ads itself: the networks are the platforms'. Only the few writes a marketer makes by hand are adapted, each named in the policy catalog. |
| Creative publishing | Not built | A reviewed asset is handed to a person who publishes it. | None. | Uploading ads or posts would put ADX's output in front of the public without the platform's own review step and the person's; the matrix marks `publish.*` unsupported for every connector. |
| Audience and conversion uploads | Not built (actions named in the policy so they can be denied) | None yet. | None. | Needs a data-processing basis for personal data upload that Reportage has not supplied; an adapter without it would be a loaded weapon. |
| Messaging (WhatsApp, email) | Integrate (adapters B6.2; sends gated by channel mode, policy, approval) | An approved draft reaches the buyer on the channel they use. | WhatsApp Cloud and SMTP adapters; Meta's template rules; no inbound. | Reportage runs WhatsApp campaigns by hand today. The adapters exist so an approved draft can go; nothing goes automatically and nothing goes until the messaging policy is supplied. Templates and inbound replies are not built because the policy that would govern them does not exist. |
| Calling | Integrate (Twilio reference adapter, ElevenLabs speech; B4.4, B4.5) | Qualification calls with a recorded reading the team can correct. | Telecom route, recording retention, speech vendor. | The UAE route is not chosen and the calling policy is unsigned; the code is a reference implementation behind a route that is empty by default. |
| Keyword and competitor research | Integrate (Google Ads keyword ideas, web fetch of public pages) | Research briefs with sources. | Keyword client, fetcher with robots respect. | ADX does not build or buy a proprietary dataset; it reads what the platform offers and what is public, and names the source on every finding. |
| Ad library and intelligence datasets | Not built | None. | None. | Scraping ad libraries or buying intelligence data is a dataset business, not a marketing tool; findings would carry a provenance ADX cannot verify. |
| Identity and roles | Integrate (authentik OIDC) with native memberships per workspace | Sign in once; a role per client. | OIDC client, membership table. | authentik already holds the people; ADX owns only who may act in which workspace. |
| Reporting mail | Integrate (SMTP) | Reports and approval links reach staff. | One relay. | A mail product is not needed for a handful of staff messages. |

## What this means for the capability matrix

`core/connections.Catalog` is the source of truth the connections screen shows. Every row above that says "not built" appears there as unsupported with its reason, so a connector's name never suggests a capability ADX lacks. Rows that say "integrate" appear as supported, with "wired" true only when the server has the configuration they need.

## Open

- Whether the team wants a richer board than stage and owner is a question for the first weeks of use, not a build decision. The native record makes either answer cheap.
- WhatsApp templates need an approved template catalog and a policy for who writes them. Until then, outside the 24-hour window, a send fails with Meta's reason and the draft is held.
